Use Tier 2: deepen the existing ConvRec with a jointly trained, gated history-pooling component. Focus on model_design and training_evaluation, leaving input splits, sampling, loss, and optimizer unchanged for a controlled experiment. The latest macro HR@10 of 0.52 remains below the best 0.5312, with Movies_and_TV also falling from the baseline’s 0.58 to 0.525. This motivates testing whether an explicit representation of persistent preferences complements the current convolution and attention features.

At each sequence position, compute the causal cumulative mean of nonpadding input item embeddings. Project this pooled vector into the backbone’s feature space and use a learned, feature-wise sigmoid gate to incorporate it into the contextual representation before the existing final normalization. Feed the resulting single representation through the existing tied item-embedding scorer and learned item bias. Train the pooling projection and gate jointly with the backbone using the unchanged next-item objective; initialize the gate toward a small contribution so the model can learn when persistent preferences help. This addresses a plausible representation bottleneck: preserving broad interests currently depends entirely on contextual layers learning to retain them.

Train one independent network per category with seed 42, and select one checkpoint per category using fixed validation HR@10 with 200 users and 99 unique negatives under evaluation seed 42. Update the predictor writer to load the added parameters strictly and use exactly the same history packing and forward computation as validation. Judge the experiment by the host’s macro-average validation HR@10, retaining all four category routes and using no checkpoint averaging, separately fitted scores, or hidden test data.
